description.text: The counter starts at 0, but clicking Increment leaves the displayed value unchanged. Fix the increment logic so every click increases the count by exactly 1. Keep the existing component state and template bindings.

solutionBlock.overview: The postfix increment expression returns the previous count. Assigning that result back to count overwrites the increment, so the value stays unchanged. Increment the property without assigning the old value back; the existing Angular click binding will update the view.

frameworkTests.name: Counter starts at zero and increments on every click

title: Fix a fleet status board from three user bug reports

description.text: Three user reports arrived for the fleet status board. Report 1: "After I pick Offline and then Online, the list goes empty even though two vehicles are online." Report 2: "When I choose Maintenance and go back to All, the empty-state message stays on screen above the full list." Report 3: "Retry sync counts two refreshes for one click." Reproduce each report from the template and component, find the root cause, and fix all three. Keep the existing test ids, the four filter buttons and the refresh counter text.

solutionBlock.overview: Report 1 is a derived-state bug: applyFilter() filters the already-filtered array instead of the full vehicles array, so every status change narrows the previous result until nothing is left. Derive filtered from vehicles every time. Report 2 is a one-way flag: showEmpty is set to true when a filter has no matches but never set back, so assign it from the filtered length on every run instead of only inside an if. Report 3 is a double handler: the Retry button is a submit button inside a form that also listens for submit, so one click runs retry() twice. Keep one handler, a type="button" with (click), and drop the form.

frameworkTests.name: Switching from Offline to Online shows the two online vehicles
The empty state disappears when a filter with results is chosen again
One Retry click counts exactly one refresh

premiumPreview.summary: Three user bug reports against one small Angular screen: a filter that narrows the wrong list, an empty state that never clears, and a button that fires twice.
learningOutcomes: Reproduce a bug from a user report before touching code.
Derive filtered state from the source list instead of from a previous result.
Spot duplicate event handlers created by form submit and click bindings.
